source_refs.note: Exercise 5.2, Question 6 (book p. 158); answer key PDF 306

blocks.prompt: 6 Find the interior angles of the quadrilateral whose vertices are \(A(2, 1)\), \(B(3, 1)\), \(C(4, 5)\) and \(D(-1, 5)\).
blocks.explanation:
Ab triangle ki jagah quadrilateral (chaar sides wali shakal) hai, lekin tareeqa bilkul wohi hai.
Chaaron sides ke slopes nikalenge, vertices ko anticlockwise ghoomenge, aur har vertex par agle vertex wali side se pichhle vertex wali side tak Theorem 7 lagayenge.
Quadrilateral ke chaaron angles ka jama \(360^\circ\) hota hai; yahi hamari tasdeeq hogi.
Plan: tarteeb check, slopes, chaar angles, jama.
Agar koi angle obtuse nikle to ghabraiye nahi; tan negative aane ka matlab sirf yeh hai ke \(180^\circ\) mein se minus karna hai.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(A(2, 1)\), \(B(3, 1)\), \(C(4, 5)\), \(D(-1, 5)\).
Maloom karna: interior angles \(A\), \(B\), \(C\), \(D\).
Tareeqa: \(A\), \(B\) neeche (baayen se daayen), \(C\), \(D\) upar (daayen se baayen), is liye \(A \to B \to C \to D\) anticlockwise hai. \(A\): \(AB\) se \(AD\) tak; \(B\): \(BC\) se \(BA\) tak; \(C\): \(CD\) se \(CB\) tak; \(D\): \(DA\) se \(DC\) tak.

Sides ke slopes
\[m_{AB} = \dfrac{1 - 1}{3 - 2} = 0\]
\[m_{BC} = \dfrac{5 - 1}{4 - 3} = 4\]
\[m_{CD} = \dfrac{5 - 5}{-1 - 4} = 0\]
\[m_{DA} = \dfrac{1 - 5}{2 - (-1)} = -\dfrac{4}{3}\]
Kyun: do points se slope. \(AB\) aur \(CD\) dono horizontal hain (slope 0), yani yeh shakal asal mein trapezium hai.
Slopes ki ek chhoti si table bana lein; har angle ke liye wahin se do values uthani hain, is se ghaltiyan kam hoti hain.

Angle \(A\) (\(AB\) se \(AD\) tak)
\[\tan A = \dfrac{-\frac{4}{3} - 0}{1 + 0} = -\dfrac{4}{3}\]
\[A = 180^\circ - 53.13^\circ = 126.87^\circ\]
Kyun: tan negative, angle obtuse; \(\tan^{-1}\frac{4}{3} = 53.13^\circ\) ko \(180^\circ\) mein se minus kiya.
Yaad rahe: quadrilateral ke andar ka angle \(180^\circ\) se bara bhi ho sakta hai sirf tab jab shakal andar ki taraf dabi hui (concave) ho; yahan aisa nahi, is liye har angle \(0^\circ\) aur \(180^\circ\) ke darmiyan hai aur tan wala tareeqa theek kaam karta hai.

Angle \(B\) (\(BC\) se \(BA\) tak)
\[\tan B = \dfrac{0 - 4}{1 + (4)(0)} = -4\]
\[B = 180^\circ - 75.96^\circ = 104.04^\circ\]
Kyun: \(m_1 = m_{BC} = 4\), \(m_2 = m_{BA} = 0\); \(\tan^{-1} 4 = 75.96^\circ\).
Dhyan dein: \(B\) par side \(BA\) baayen ja rahi hai aur \(BC\) tez upar daayen; is liye angle \(90^\circ\) se bara hona hi chahiye. Answer key yahin ghalat hai.

Angle \(C\) (\(CD\) se \(CB\) tak)
\[\tan C = \dfrac{4 - 0}{1 + (0)(4)} = 4\]
\[C = \tan^{-1} 4 = 75.96^\circ\]
Kyun: \(m_1 = m_{CD} = 0\), \(m_2 = m_{CB} = 4\).
Ghaur karein: \(B\) aur \(C\) par wahi number 4 aaya, sirf sign ulta; is liye ek angle doosre ka supplementary hai.

Tasdeeq:
\[126.87^\circ + 104.04^\circ + 75.96^\circ + 53.13^\circ = 360^\circ \;\checkmark\]
Saath hi \(AB \parallel DC\) hai, is liye co-interior angles ka jama \(180^\circ\): \(A + D = 180^\circ\) aur \(B + C = 180^\circ\); dono sahi nikle.
Khulasa: chaar angles mein se do obtuse (\(A\), \(B\)) aur do acute (\(C\), \(D\)) hain. Neeche wali side \(AB\) chhoti (lambai 1) aur upar wali \(DC\) lambi (lambai 5) hai, is liye neeche ke angles bare hain; figure bana kar dekhein to yeh saaf nazar aata hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key \(126.9^\circ, 74^\circ, 106^\circ, 53.1^\circ\) chhapti hai. \(B\) aur \(C\) ke angles ghalat hain: \(\tan B = -4\) se \(B = 104.0^\circ\) (obtuse) aur \(\tan C = 4\) se \(C = 76.0^\circ\). Kyunke \(AB \parallel DC\), \(B + C = 180^\circ\) hona chahiye, aur \(104.0^\circ + 76.0^\circ = 180^\circ\). Sahi: \(126.9^\circ, 104.0^\circ, 76.0^\circ, 53.1^\circ\).
